“Not under conscious control” and “external” are not the same thing. Lots of internal processes are automatic and don’t obey deliberate will:
- a thought popping in unexpectedly,
- a memory surfacing,
- a tune getting stuck,
- noticing a word everywhere once it’s salient,
- body sensations you can’t summon or dismiss.

Those can feel independent of you while still coming from your own mind/brain.

Also, “I can’t make it happen by trying” doesn’t prove it’s external. Plenty of internal things are nonvoluntary. And “I can’t push it away” doesn’t prove externality either; unwanted thoughts are famously hard to suppress.

The key question is evidence. If something is external, there should usually be some observation that distinguishes it from an internal pattern:
- can other people verify it?
- does it persist in a way independent of your interpretation?
- does it predict something measurable?
- can it be checked when you’re not the one noticing it?

If you want, give me one concrete example: the exact number or word, how often it appears, and over what time window. I can help you test the claim carefully, without assuming it’s “all in your head” or assuming it’s external either.
